children: The $100-billion-plus FCNR-B deposit deluge will not trigger an abrupt surge in bank lending, SBI Chairman CS Setty said on Wednesday, with banks likely to take three to four months to deploy the funds.

Speaking on the sidelines of the Global Fintech Fest, Setty said the funds raised through the FCNR-B route would take "three or four months" to be deployed into lending. SBI has not disclosed its FCNR-B inflows, although estimates peg them at nearly $10 billion.
“I don’t think the FCNR-B inflows we have gotten will lead to any sort of abnormal lending… it’ll take at least three to four months to deploy these inflows into the banking system,” Setty said.

Surprisingly, this contrasts sharply with what Axis Bank’s Chief Executive Officer Amitabh Chaudhry said on Wednesday: a significant amount of dollars in the system could lead to abnormal lending to some extent, although he also said it would take quite some time to deploy all the funds through lending.

According to recent data from the RBI, the inflows through the FCNR-B route touched $127.2 billion as at the end of August 31, nearly 7X of what was garnered in 2013, which was around $26 billion. Taking into account the external commercial borrowings (ECBs) and overseas foreign currency borrowings (OFCBs), the total inflows came up to $136.4 billion.
SBI a early adopter of AI and ML tools

Setty gave a keynote address during the fintech event, where he outlined the use-cases for artificial intelligence in banking, and that SBI has been one of the early adopters of AI and machine learning tools across workplace functions.

“Customer service was one of the early visible applications through AI. We are using conventional AI based approaches in credit assesment and cashflow based lending. We are also now moving towards next generational AI capabilities, which are going to be different,” he said.
He further flagged that while the initial fixed costs can be expensive for agentic AI agents, the incremental costs can be low, creating economic efficiency.
Setty called for trust to be embedded within agentic AI models. “The moment AI moves from recommendation to execution, accountability becomes even more important,” Setty said.

title: FCNR-B inflows won't trigger abrupt lending; 3-4 months needed to deploy funds, says SBI Chief CS Setty at GFF
